name: Eden
what: The region where God planted a garden and placed the first man and woman.
today: Exact location unknown; Genesis links it with the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.
key: God planted a garden in Eden and put the man there to work it and keep it (Genesis 2).
After they sinned, God sent Adam and Eve out of Eden and placed cherubim to guard the way (Genesis 3).
God promised to make Zion's wilderness like Eden (Isaiah 51).
Ezekiel described the king of Tyre as having been in Eden, the garden of God (Ezekiel 28).
Joel pictured the land as Eden before the invading army and a desolate wilderness behind it (Joel 2).

name: Gihon
what: One of the four rivers flowing out of Eden, said to wind through the land of Cush.
today: Exact location unknown; one of the rivers of Eden.
key: A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden and divided into four rivers (Genesis 2).
The second river, the Gihon, flows around the whole land of Cush (Genesis 2).

name: Gomer
what: A distant northern people and land descended from Japheth, named among Gog's allies.
today: Likely central Turkey, home of the ancient Cimmerians.
key: Gomer is listed as the first son of Japheth, ancestor of a northern people (Genesis 10).
Gomer and all its hordes are named among Gog's allies from the far north (Ezekiel 38).

name: Hazor
what: A group of Arabian desert settlements, named with Kedar in Jeremiah's oracles; not the Canaanite city.
today: Exact site unknown; in the Arabian desert east of Israel.
key: Jeremiah announced that Nebuchadnezzar would strike Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor (Jeremiah 49).
The people of Hazor were told to flee far away and hide (Jeremiah 49).
Hazor would become a haunt of jackals, desolate forever (Jeremiah 49).

name: Holy Place
what: The outer room of the tabernacle, in front of the veil that screened off the Most Holy Place.
today: The tabernacle was a portable tent; it no longer exists.
key: The veil divided the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place, with the table and lampstand outside it (Exodus 26).
Golden bells on Aaron's robe sounded whenever he entered the Holy Place before the Lord (Exodus 28).
The incense altar stood before the veil, and Aaron burned incense there every morning (Exodus 30).
Moses placed the table, lampstand, and golden altar in the tent before the veil (Exodus 40).

name: Judah
what: The territory of the tribe of Judah, including its hill country, wilderness, and Negeb south of Jerusalem.
today: The southern West Bank and southern Israel, around Bethlehem and Hebron.
key: Joshua wiped out the Anakim from the hill country of Judah (Joshua 11).
Judah's boundaries and towns were set out by lot (Joshua 15).
Men of Judah bound Samson and handed him over to the Philistines (Judges 15).
The prophet Gad told David to leave his stronghold and go into the land of Judah (1 Samuel 22).
David wrote a psalm of longing for God while in the wilderness of Judah (Psalm 63).

name: Most Holy Place
what: The innermost room of the tabernacle, and later of the temple, where the ark of the covenant stood.
today: No longer exists; the temple stood on the Temple Mount, Jerusalem.
key: A veil separated the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place, where the ark was placed (Exodus 26).
The high priest entered behind the veil only once a year, on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16).
Solomon built the temple's Most Holy Place and overlaid it with fine gold (2 Chronicles 3).
When Jesus died, the temple curtain was torn in two from top to bottom (Matthew 27).
Christ entered the holy places once for all by his own blood (Hebrews 9).

name: Elkosh
what: The hometown of the prophet Nahum, who is called the Elkoshite.
today: Exact site unknown.
key: The book of Nahum is the vision of Nahum of Elkosh concerning Nineveh (Nahum 1).
Nahum announced that the LORD would make a complete end of Nineveh (Nahum 1).

name: Nehelam
what: The home or family of Shemaiah, a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon.
today: Exact site unknown.
key: The LORD gave Jeremiah a message for Shemaiah of Nehelam among the exiles (Jeremiah 29).
Shemaiah had written to the priest Zephaniah, urging him to confine Jeremiah (Jeremiah 29).
The LORD said Shemaiah prophesied unsent and would have no descendant among the people (Jeremiah 29).

name: Sheba
what: A wealthy kingdom in southern Arabia, known for gold, spices, and incense.
today: Likely Yemen, southwestern Arabia
key: The queen of Sheba visited Solomon to test him with hard questions (1 Kings 10).
The psalmist prays that the kings of Sheba will bring gifts (Psalms 72).
Isaiah foresaw people from Sheba bringing gold and frankincense (Isaiah 60).
Merchants of Sheba traded spices, gems, and gold with Tyre (Ezekiel 27).

name: Sephar
what: A place in the hill country of the east, marking the limit of the lands of Joktan's descendants.
today: Possibly in southern Arabia; exact site unknown.
key: Joktan's descendants lived from Mesha in the direction of Sephar (Genesis 10).
Sephar is described as the hill country of the east (Genesis 10).

name: Cush
what: The land south of Egypt along the upper Nile.
today: Sudan and southern Egypt (ancient Nubia)
key: Tirhakah king of Cush marched out against Sennacherib (2 Kings 19).
The psalmist says Cush will stretch out its hands to God (Psalms 68).
Isaiah walked barefoot as a sign against Egypt and Cush (Isaiah 20).
Zephaniah foresaw worshipers bringing offerings from beyond the rivers of Cush (Zephaniah 3).

name: Cush
what: An ancient land south of Egypt, marking the far edge of the known world in biblical times.
today: Mainly modern Sudan, south of Egypt; not modern Ethiopia.
key: The river Gihon flows around the whole land of Cush (Genesis 2).
King Ahasuerus rules 127 provinces from India to Cush (Esther 1).
Mordecai's decree goes to every province from India to Cush (Esther 8).
Job says the topaz of Cush cannot equal the worth of wisdom (Job 28).

name: Ophir
what: A distant land famous for its fine gold, reached by ship.
today: Exact site unknown; possibly southern Arabia, East Africa, or India.
key: Solomon's fleet with Hiram's sailors brought gold from Ophir (1 Kings 9).
Hiram's ships also brought almug wood and precious stones from Ophir (1 Kings 10).
Jehoshaphat's ships bound for Ophir were wrecked at Ezion-geber (1 Kings 22).
David gave gold of Ophir for building the temple (1 Chronicles 29).
Job says wisdom cannot be bought with the gold of Ophir (Job 28).

name: India
what: The eastern edge of the Persian Empire, along the Indus River valley.
today: The Indus Valley region, in modern Pakistan and northwestern India.
key: King Ahasuerus ruled 127 provinces from India to Cush (Esther 1).
Mordecai's decree allowing the Jews to defend themselves went to every province from India to Cush (Esther 8).

name: Syene
what: A town at Egypt's southern frontier on the Nile, marking the far limit of Egypt.
today: Aswan, in southern Egypt.
key: Isaiah foresees God's people gathering from distant places, including the land of Syene (Isaiah 49).
God promises to make Egypt desolate from Migdol to Syene (Ezekiel 29).
Ezekiel says Egypt's helpers will fall by the sword from Migdol to Syene (Ezekiel 30).

name: Thebes
what: A great ancient capital of Upper Egypt and center of the worship of the god Amon.
today: Luxor, in southern Egypt.
key: The Lord announces he will punish Amon of Thebes along with Pharaoh and Egypt (Jeremiah 46).
Ezekiel prophesies that God will execute judgments on Thebes and cut off its multitude (Ezekiel 30).
Nahum warns Nineveh that mighty Thebes was still carried into exile (Nahum 3).

name: Dedan
what: An Arabian trading people and oasis region southeast of Edom.
today: The al-Ula area of northwestern Saudi Arabia.
key: Dedan was among the nations made to drink the cup of God's wrath (Jeremiah 25).
Jeremiah warned the people of Dedan to flee from Edom's disaster (Jeremiah 49).
Ezekiel foretold Edom's ruin from Teman even to Dedan (Ezekiel 25).
Dedan traded saddlecloths with Tyre (Ezekiel 27).
Sheba and Dedan question Gog's plan to plunder (Ezekiel 38).

name: Red Sea
what: The sea between Egypt and Arabia that God parted for Israel to escape Pharaoh.
today: Red Sea, including the Gulfs of Suez and Aqaba; exact crossing site debated
key: God drove the locusts of the eighth plague into the Red Sea (Exodus 10).
Pharaoh's chariots and army were drowned in the Red Sea (Exodus 15).
Rahab told the spies that Jericho had heard how God dried up the Red Sea (Joshua 2).
Solomon built a fleet at Ezion-geber on the shore of the Red Sea (1 Kings 9).
By faith Israel crossed the Red Sea as on dry land (Hebrews 11).

name: Kedar
what: An Arabian desert people and region descended from Ishmael's son Kedar.
today: The north Arabian desert, in modern Saudi Arabia and Jordan.
key: The psalmist laments dwelling among the tents of Kedar (Psalm 120).
The bride compares herself to the dark tents of Kedar (Song of Solomon 1).
Isaiah foresaw the flocks of Kedar gathered to Zion (Isaiah 60).
Jeremiah announced that Nebuchadnezzar would strike Kedar (Jeremiah 49).
Kedar's princes traded lambs, rams, and goats with Tyre (Ezekiel 27).

name: Arabia
what: The desert lands east and south of Israel, home to nomadic tribes and trading peoples.
today: The Arabian Peninsula; in Galatians likely the Nabatean region of Jordan and northwestern Saudi Arabia.
key: The kings of Arabia brought gold and silver to Solomon (2 Chronicles 9).
Isaiah delivered an oracle concerning Arabia (Isaiah 21).
Arabia and Kedar traded lambs, rams, and goats with Tyre (Ezekiel 27).
After his conversion Paul went away into Arabia (Galatians 1).
Paul wrote that Mount Sinai is in Arabia (Galatians 4).

name: Dumah
what: An oasis region in northern Arabia, the subject of a brief oracle in Isaiah.
today: Likely Dumat al-Jandal (al-Jawf), northern Saudi Arabia.
key: Dumah is named as a son of Ishmael, whose descendants likely gave the oasis its name (Genesis 25).
In an oracle concerning Dumah, someone calls from Seir asking the watchman about the night (Isaiah 21).
The watchman answers that morning comes, and also the night (Isaiah 21).

name: Tema
what: An oasis town in northern Arabia on major caravan routes, settled by descendants of Ishmael.
today: Tayma, in northwestern Saudi Arabia.
key: Job compares his friends to dry streams that disappoint the caravans of Tema (Job 6).
The inhabitants of Tema are told to bring water and bread to fugitives (Isaiah 21).
Tema is among the nations made to drink the cup of God's wrath (Jeremiah 25).

name: Pathros
what: Upper Egypt, the southern part of the Nile Valley.
today: Upper (southern) Egypt, along the Nile.
key: Isaiah foretold God gathering his remnant from Pathros (Isaiah 11).
Jeremiah rebuked the Jews living in Pathros for idolatry (Jeremiah 44).
Ezekiel foretold Egypt's return to Pathros, their land of origin (Ezekiel 29).
Ezekiel announced that Pathros would be made desolate (Ezekiel 30).

name: Mount Sinai
what: The mountain in the wilderness where God gave Israel his law and made his covenant with them.
today: Traditionally Jebel Musa, southern Sinai Peninsula, Egypt; exact site debated
key: The LORD descended on Mount Sinai in fire as Israel trembled below (Exodus 19).
Moses stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights (Exodus 24).
God gave Moses the two tablets of the testimony on Mount Sinai (Exodus 31).
Moses came down with new tablets, his face shining (Exodus 34).
Paul compares Hagar to Mount Sinai, representing the old covenant (Galatians 4).

name: Sinai
what: The wilderness around Mount Sinai, where Israel camped for about a year after the exodus.
today: Southern Sinai Peninsula, Egypt
key: Israel traveled through the wilderness of Sin, between Elim and Sinai (Exodus 16).
Israel arrived in the wilderness of Sinai and camped before the mountain (Exodus 19).
Moses counted the men of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai (Numbers 1).
Israel kept the Passover in the wilderness of Sinai (Numbers 9).
The cloud lifted, and Israel set out from the wilderness of Sinai (Numbers 10).

name: Horeb
what: Another name for Mount Sinai, the mountain of God where the LORD made his covenant with Israel.
today: Traditionally Jebel Musa, southern Sinai Peninsula, Egypt; exact site debated
key: God spoke to Moses from a burning bush at Horeb (Exodus 3).
Moses struck the rock at Horeb, and water came out for the people (Exodus 17).
The LORD made his covenant with Israel at Horeb (Deuteronomy 5).
Elijah fled to Horeb and heard the LORD in a low whisper (1 Kings 19).
Malachi called Israel to remember the law given at Horeb (Malachi 4).

name: Rephidim
what: An Israelite camp in the wilderness shortly before Mount Sinai.
today: Exact site unknown; possibly Wadi Feiran in southern Sinai.
key: God gave water from the rock at Rephidim, and Israel defeated Amalek (Exodus 17).
Israel set out from Rephidim and came to the wilderness of Sinai (Exodus 19).
Rephidim appears in the list of wilderness stages (Numbers 33).

name: Massah
what: A place near Rephidim where Israel tested the Lord by demanding water.
today: Near Rephidim in the Sinai Peninsula; exact site unknown.
key: Israel quarrels and tests the Lord over water, so Moses names the place Massah and Meribah (Exodus 17).
Moses warns Israel not to put the Lord to the test as at Massah (Deuteronomy 6).
Moses recalls that Israel provoked the Lord at Massah (Deuteronomy 9).
Moses' blessing on Levi recalls God testing him at Massah (Deuteronomy 33).

name: Meribah
what: A place near Rephidim where Israel quarreled with Moses and tested the Lord over water.
today: Near Rephidim in the Sinai Peninsula; exact site unknown.
key: God brought water from the rock at Horeb, and Moses named the place Massah and Meribah (Exodus 17).
Moses' blessing on Levi recalls God contending with him at the waters of Meribah (Deuteronomy 33).

name: Wilderness of Sin
what: A wilderness between Elim and Mount Sinai where God first gave Israel manna and quail.
today: Likely in the southwestern Sinai Peninsula, Egypt; exact site uncertain.
key: Israel grumbles in the wilderness of Sin, and God provides quail and manna (Exodus 16).
Israel moves on from the wilderness of Sin to Rephidim (Exodus 17).
The wilderness of Sin is recorded among Israel's camps (Numbers 33).

name: Mesha
what: A place marking one end of the territory where the descendants of Joktan lived.
today: Exact site unknown; possibly in Arabia.
key: Joktan's sons lived from Mesha in the direction of Sephar, the hill country of the east (Genesis 10).
Joktan, a descendant of Shem through Eber, had thirteen sons, including Sheba, Ophir, and Havilah (Genesis 10).

name: Hazeroth
what: An Israelite camp in the Sinai wilderness after leaving Mount Sinai.
today: Exact site unknown; possibly 'Ain Khadra in eastern Sinai.
key: Israel traveled from Kibroth-hattaavah to Hazeroth (Numbers 11).
At Hazeroth Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses, and Miriam became leprous (Numbers 12).
Hazeroth appears in the list of wilderness stages (Numbers 33).
Moses' final speeches name Hazeroth as a landmark (Deuteronomy 1).

name: Kibroth-hattaavah
what: A wilderness camp whose name means graves of craving, where Israel craved meat.
today: Exact site unknown; in the Sinai wilderness.
key: God sent quail and then a plague on those who craved meat (Numbers 11).
Kibroth-hattaavah appears in the list of wilderness stages (Numbers 33).
Moses recalled Israel provoking the LORD there (Deuteronomy 9).

name: Taberah
what: A wilderness camp where fire from the Lord burned among the complaining Israelites.
today: Exact site unknown; in the wilderness between Mount Sinai and Kadesh.
key: When the people complained, fire from the Lord burned the outskirts of the camp (Numbers 11).
Moses prayed, the fire died down, and the place was named Taberah (Numbers 11).
Moses reminds Israel that they provoked the Lord at Taberah, Massah, and Kibroth-hattaavah (Deuteronomy 9).

name: Midian
what: The desert homeland of the Midianites, east of the Gulf of Aqaba.
today: Likely northwestern Saudi Arabia
key: Moses fled from Pharaoh to the land of Midian (Exodus 2).
Moses tended the flock of Jethro, the priest of Midian (Exodus 3).
Phinehas killed an Israelite man and a Midianite woman, stopping the plague (Numbers 25).
Gideon and three hundred men routed the Midianite army (Judges 7).

name: Paran
what: A wilderness region between Sinai and Canaan, south of the Negev.
today: The east-central Sinai Peninsula, Egypt.
key: Ishmael grew up in the wilderness of Paran (Genesis 21).
Leaving Sinai, the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran (Numbers 10).
Moses sent the twelve spies from the wilderness of Paran (Numbers 13).
After Samuel's death, David went down to the wilderness of Paran (1 Samuel 25).
Hadad the Edomite passed through Paran while fleeing to Egypt (1 Kings 11).

name: Elim
what: An oasis in the wilderness with twelve springs and seventy palm trees, where Israel camped after the Red Sea.
today: Possibly Wadi Gharandel, in western Sinai, Egypt.
key: Israel camps at Elim beside twelve springs and seventy palm trees (Exodus 15).
Israel sets out from Elim into the wilderness of Sin (Exodus 16).
Elim is recorded among Israel's wilderness camps (Numbers 33).

name: Marah
what: A place in the wilderness of Shur whose name means bitter, for its undrinkable water.
today: Exact site unknown; possibly Ain Hawarah in western Sinai.
key: At Marah the water was bitter until the LORD showed Moses a log that made it sweet (Exodus 15).
Marah is listed as Israel's campsite after three days in the wilderness (Numbers 33).

name: Elath
what: A port town at the northern tip of the Gulf of Aqaba, contested between Judah and Edom.
today: Near modern Eilat, Israel, and Aqaba, Jordan.
key: Israel passed by Elath and Ezion-geber on its way around Edom (Deuteronomy 2).
King Azariah rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah (2 Kings 14).
In Ahaz's day Rezin recovered Elath for Edom and drove out the people of Judah (2 Kings 16).

name: Eloth
what: Another spelling of Elath, a port on the Gulf of Aqaba near Ezion-geber.
today: Near modern Eilat, Israel, and Aqaba, Jordan.
key: Solomon built a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber near Eloth on the Red Sea (1 Kings 9).
The Chronicler repeats that Solomon went to Ezion-geber and Eloth by the sea (2 Chronicles 8).
King Uzziah rebuilt Eloth and restored it to Judah (2 Chronicles 26).

name: Ezion-geber
what: A port at the northern tip of the Gulf of Aqaba, on the Red Sea.
today: Near Eilat and Aqaba; possibly Tell el-Kheleifeh.
key: Israel camped at Ezion-geber during the wilderness journey (Numbers 33).
Israel passed by Elath and Ezion-geber, going around Edom (Deuteronomy 2).
Solomon built a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber (1 Kings 9).
Jehoshaphat's ships were wrecked at Ezion-geber, as Eliezer had prophesied (2 Chronicles 20).

name: Jotbathah
what: A campsite of Israel in the wilderness, described as a land with brooks of water.
today: Exact site unknown; possibly near the Gulf of Aqaba.
key: Israel set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah (Numbers 33).
Moses recalls Jotbathah as a land with brooks of water (Deuteronomy 10).

name: Memphis
what: An ancient royal city of Egypt near the head of the Nile Delta.
today: Ruins at Mit Rahina, south of Cairo, Egypt.
key: Isaiah said the princes of Memphis were deluded (Isaiah 19).
Jeremiah addressed Judeans who had fled to Egypt and were living in Memphis (Jeremiah 44).
Jeremiah warned that Memphis would become a waste (Jeremiah 46).
Ezekiel announced that God would destroy the idols of Memphis (Ezekiel 30).
Hosea warned that Memphis would bury Israelites who fled to Egypt (Hosea 9).

name: Baal-zephon
what: A landmark in Egypt near the sea, where Israel camped just before crossing the Red Sea.
today: Exact site unknown; in northeastern Egypt near the Red Sea crossing.
key: God told Israel to camp facing Baal-zephon, and Pharaoh's army overtook them there by the sea (Exodus 14).
Baal-zephon is listed on Moses' record of Israel's journey out of Egypt (Numbers 33).

name: Pi-hahiroth
what: A campsite in Egypt between Migdol and the sea, where Israel stopped before crossing.
today: Exact site unknown; in northeastern Egypt near the Red Sea crossing.
key: God had Israel camp before Pi-hahiroth, where Pharaoh's army overtook them (Exodus 14).
From Pi-hahiroth Israel passed through the sea into the wilderness (Numbers 33).

name: Migdol
what: A fortified place on Egypt's northeastern frontier, named in the exodus and later a home of Jewish refugees.
today: Likely in the northeastern Nile Delta near Sinai; exact site uncertain.
key: God told Israel to camp between Migdol and the sea before crossing (Exodus 14).
Israel's camp near Migdol appears in the list of wilderness stages (Numbers 33).
Jeremiah addressed Jews living in Migdol and other Egyptian towns (Jeremiah 44).
Ezekiel foretold Egypt's desolation from Migdol to Syene (Ezekiel 29).

name: Uz
what: The land where Job lived, apparently east of Israel and associated with Edom.
today: Exact site unknown; likely east or southeast of the Dead Sea.
key: Job, a blameless man who feared God, lived in the land of Uz (Job 1).
The kings of the land of Uz are among those made to drink God's cup of wrath (Jeremiah 25).
Lamentations addresses Edom as dwelling in the land of Uz, warning that judgment will reach her (Lamentations 4).

name: Nile
what: The great river of Egypt, the source of the country's life and farming.
today: Nile River, Egypt
key: Pharaoh dreamed of seven cows coming up out of the Nile (Genesis 41).
Pharaoh ordered every newborn Hebrew boy thrown into the Nile (Exodus 1).
Moses struck the Nile, and its water turned to blood (Exodus 7).
Frogs came up from the Nile and covered Egypt (Exodus 8).
God judged Pharaoh, who claimed to have made the Nile for himself (Ezekiel 29).

name: Egypt
what: The great kingdom of the Nile valley, where Israel grew into a nation and was later enslaved.
today: Egypt
key: Abram went down to Egypt during a famine in Canaan (Genesis 12).
Joseph, sold by his brothers, rose to rule over all Egypt under Pharaoh (Genesis 41).
Jacob and his whole family moved to Egypt and settled in Goshen (Genesis 46).
After the tenth plague, the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt on Passover night (Exodus 12).
Joseph took Mary and the child Jesus to Egypt to escape Herod (Matthew 2).

name: On
what: An ancient Egyptian city and center of sun worship, home of Joseph's father-in-law.
today: Heliopolis, in northeastern Cairo, Egypt.
key: Pharaoh gives Joseph Asenath, daughter of Potiphera priest of On, as his wife (Genesis 41).
Asenath of On bears Joseph's sons Manasseh and Ephraim (Genesis 46).
Ezekiel foretells that the young men of On will fall by the sword (Ezekiel 30).

name: Rahab
what: A poetic name for Egypt, also used of a sea monster symbolizing forces God subdues.
today: Egypt, used as a poetic name.
key: God lists Rahab, meaning Egypt, among nations whose people will be counted in Zion (Psalms 87).
The psalmist praises God, who crushed Rahab and scattered his enemies (Psalms 89).
Isaiah recalls the LORD's arm that cut Rahab in pieces, recalling the exodus (Isaiah 51).

name: Havilah
what: A desert region at the eastern edge of the Ishmaelite and Amalekite lands, toward Arabia.
today: Exact location unknown; likely in northwestern Arabia.
key: Ishmael's descendants settled from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt (Genesis 25).
Saul defeated the Amalekites from Havilah as far as Shur (1 Samuel 15).

name: Teman
what: A region or town in Edom, known for its wise men and warriors.
today: Southern Jordan, in ancient Edom; exact site unknown.
key: Jeremiah asked whether wisdom was gone from Teman (Jeremiah 49).
Ezekiel foretold desolation from Teman to Dedan (Ezekiel 25).
Amos announced fire on Teman (Amos 1).
Obadiah warned that Teman's mighty men would be dismayed (Obadiah 1).
Habakkuk saw God coming from Teman in glory (Habakkuk 3).

name: Shur
what: A desert region in northwestern Sinai along Egypt's eastern frontier.
today: Northwestern Sinai, east of the Suez region of Egypt.
key: The angel of the LORD found Hagar by a spring on the way to Shur (Genesis 16).
Abraham lived between Kadesh and Shur and sojourned in Gerar (Genesis 20).
After crossing the Red Sea, Israel went three days into the wilderness of Shur (Exodus 15).
Saul defeated the Amalekites from Havilah as far as Shur (1 Samuel 15).
David raided peoples living toward Shur while among the Philistines (1 Samuel 27).

name: Negeb
what: The dry southern region of Judah, stretching south from Hebron toward the Sinai.
today: Negev desert, southern Israel
key: Abram journeyed by stages toward the Negeb (Genesis 12).
Isaac was living in the Negeb when Rebekah arrived (Genesis 24).
Moses told the spies to go up into the Negeb and the hill country (Numbers 13).
Joshua struck the whole land, including the Negeb (Joshua 10).
David told Achish he had raided the Negeb of Judah (1 Samuel 27).

name: Mount Hor
what: A mountain on the border of Edom where Aaron died.
today: Exact site unknown; traditionally Jebel Harun near Petra, Jordan.
key: Aaron died on Mount Hor after his garments were placed on his son Eleazar (Numbers 20).
Israel set out from Mount Hor to go around Edom (Numbers 21).
Aaron died on Mount Hor at age 123, in the fortieth year after the exodus (Numbers 33).
God told Moses he would die on Nebo as Aaron died on Mount Hor (Deuteronomy 32).

name: Moserah
what: A wilderness camp of Israel, where Deuteronomy records that Aaron died and was buried.
today: Exact site unknown; near the border of Edom.
key: Israel journeyed from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried (Deuteronomy 10).
From there Israel journeyed to Gudgodah and then to Jotbathah (Deuteronomy 10).

name: Bene-jaakan
what: A wilderness campsite of Israel, also called the wells of the Bene-jaakan, near Moserah.
today: Exact site unknown; in the wilderness south of Canaan.
key: Israel set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan (Numbers 33).
From Bene-jaakan they moved on and camped at Hor-haggidgad (Numbers 33).
Moses recalled Israel journeying from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah, where Aaron died (Deuteronomy 10).

name: Sela
what: A rocky stronghold in Edom; the name means rock.
today: Possibly Petra or nearby as-Sela in southern Jordan.
key: The border of the Amorites ran from the ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela upward (Judges 1).
Moab's refugees are told to send lambs to Zion from Sela (Isaiah 16).
Isaiah calls the inhabitants of Sela to sing for joy to the LORD (Isaiah 42).

name: Nebaioth
what: The desert territory of an Arabian tribe descended from Ishmael's firstborn son Nebaioth.
today: Northern Arabia; exact area uncertain.
key: Nebaioth, Ishmael's firstborn son, gave his name to the tribe (Genesis 25).
Isaiah foresees the rams of Nebaioth accepted on God's altar (Isaiah 60).

name: Hor-haggidgad
what: One of Israel's campsites during the wilderness wanderings, between Bene-jaakan and Jotbathah.
today: Exact site unknown; in the wilderness south of the Dead Sea, possibly in the Arabah.
key: Israel set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad (Numbers 33).
From Hor-haggidgad they moved on and camped at Jotbathah (Numbers 33).
Moses recalled the journey from Moserah to Gudgodah and on to Jotbathah (Deuteronomy 10).

name: Etham
what: A camp on the edge of the wilderness on Israel's route out of Egypt.
today: Exact site unknown; on the eastern edge of the Nile Delta, Egypt.
key: Israel moves from Succoth and camps at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness (Exodus 13).
Israel camps at Etham and later travels three days in the wilderness of Etham (Numbers 33).

name: Succoth
what: The first camp of Israel after leaving Rameses at the exodus.
today: Likely Tell el-Maskhuta, in the eastern Nile Delta, Egypt.
key: About six hundred thousand men on foot journey from Rameses to Succoth (Exodus 12).
Israel sets out from Succoth and camps at Etham (Exodus 13).
Succoth is recorded as Israel's first camp after Rameses (Numbers 33).

name: Amalek
what: The territory of the Amalekites, a nomadic people of the Negeb and Sinai who attacked Israel.
today: Negev and northern Sinai, approximately
key: Israel defeated Amalek at Rephidim while Moses' hands were held up (Exodus 17).
Moses commanded Israel to blot out the memory of Amalek (Deuteronomy 25).
Saul defeated Amalek but spared King Agag and the best livestock (1 Samuel 15).
David dedicated to the LORD the spoil taken from Amalek (2 Samuel 8).

name: Kadesh
what: An oasis in the wilderness south of Canaan, where Israel camped for many years.
today: Likely Ein el-Qudeirat, northeastern Sinai, Egypt
key: Abraham lived for a time between Kadesh and Shur (Genesis 20).
The twelve spies returned to Moses at Kadesh with their report (Numbers 13).
Miriam died at Kadesh, and Moses struck the rock for water (Numbers 20).
Israel remained at Kadesh many days after refusing to enter the land (Deuteronomy 1).

name: Kadesh-barnea
what: An oasis on the southern edge of Canaan where Israel camped during the wilderness years.
today: Likely Ein el-Qudeirat in northeastern Sinai, Egypt.
key: Moses sent the spies from Kadesh-barnea to see the land (Numbers 32).
Kadesh-barnea marked the southern boundary of the Promised Land (Numbers 34).
Israel rebelled at Kadesh-barnea, refusing to go up into the land (Deuteronomy 9).
Joshua struck down cities from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza (Joshua 10).
Caleb recalled being sent from Kadesh-barnea as a spy at age forty (Joshua 14).

name: Zin
what: A desert region south of Canaan around Kadesh, where Israel wandered and camped.
today: The desert of southern Israel and northeastern Sinai, near Kadesh-barnea.
key: The twelve spies began exploring Canaan from the wilderness of Zin (Numbers 13).
Miriam died at Kadesh in Zin, and Moses struck the rock at Meribah (Numbers 20).
God reminded Moses that he had rebelled in the wilderness of Zin (Numbers 27).
Zin marked the southern border of Canaan and of Judah (Numbers 34).
Judah's southern boundary passed along the wilderness of Zin (Joshua 15).

name: Meribah
what: The waters at Kadesh where Moses struck the rock and Israel quarreled with the Lord.
today: Near Kadesh-barnea, in the northeastern Sinai Peninsula.
key: Moses strikes the rock, and the waters are named Meribah because Israel quarreled (Numbers 20).
God recalls that Moses and Aaron rebelled at the waters of Meribah of Kadesh (Numbers 27).
God recalls testing Israel at the waters of Meribah (Psalms 81).

name: Meribah-kadesh
what: The waters at Kadesh where Moses and Aaron failed to honor God before Israel.
today: Likely near Kadesh-barnea, at Ain el-Qudeirat in northeastern Sinai.
key: God told Moses he would not enter the land because he broke faith at Meribah-kadesh (Deuteronomy 32).
In Ezekiel's vision, Meribah-kadesh marks the southern border of the restored land (Ezekiel 47).
The southern boundary of the tribal allotments again runs to Meribah-kadesh (Ezekiel 48).

name: Zin
what: A desert region south of Canaan around Kadesh, forming the southern border of the land.
today: The desert of southern Israel and northeastern Sinai, near Kadesh-barnea.
key: The twelve spies began exploring Canaan from the wilderness of Zin (Numbers 13).
Miriam died at Kadesh in Zin, and Moses struck the rock at Meribah (Numbers 20).
Zin marked the southern border of Canaan and of Judah (Numbers 34).
Judah's southern boundary passed along the wilderness of Zin (Joshua 15).

name: Akrabbim
what: A steep ascent marking the southern border of the promised land and of Judah.
today: Likely Ma'ale Akrabim (Scorpion Pass), in the Negev, southern Israel.
key: The southern boundary of the land runs south of the ascent of Akrabbim (Numbers 34).
Judah's southern boundary passes south of the ascent of Akrabbim (Joshua 15).
The Amorites' border runs from the ascent of Akrabbim (Judges 1).

name: Goshen
what: A fertile region of Egypt where Jacob's family settled.
today: The eastern Nile Delta of Egypt, likely around Wadi Tumilat.
key: Joseph invited his father to live in Goshen, near him (Genesis 45).
Joseph met his father Jacob in Goshen (Genesis 46).
Pharaoh granted Jacob's family the land of Goshen for their flocks (Genesis 47).
God kept the swarms of flies out of Goshen, where Israel lived (Exodus 8).
Hail struck Egypt, but not the land of Goshen (Exodus 9).

name: Edom
what: The land of Esau's descendants, south and southeast of the Dead Sea.
today: Southern Jordan
key: Esau, also called Edom, settled in the hill country of Seir (Genesis 36).
The king of Edom refused to let Israel pass through his land (Numbers 20).
David put garrisons throughout Edom, and the Edomites became his servants (2 Samuel 8).
Edom revolted from Judah and set up its own king (2 Kings 8).
Obadiah announced judgment on Edom for its violence against Jacob (Obadiah 1).

name: Seir
what: The mountainous land south of the Dead Sea where Esau's descendants, the Edomites, lived.
today: Mountains of southern Jordan, east of the Arabah
key: Jacob sent messengers to his brother Esau in the land of Seir (Genesis 32).
After meeting Jacob, Esau returned to Seir (Genesis 33).
God gave Mount Seir to Esau and told Israel not to fight them (Deuteronomy 2).
Men of Mount Seir were destroyed when their allies turned on them (2 Chronicles 20).

name: Mount Seir
what: The mountainous region of Edom, given to Esau's descendants.
today: The mountains of southern Jordan, east of the Arabah valley.
key: Israel traveled around Mount Seir for many days (Deuteronomy 2).
God gave Mount Seir to Esau and forbade Israel to take it (Deuteronomy 2).
Simeonites went to Mount Seir and destroyed the remaining Amalekites (1 Chronicles 4).
Men of Mount Seir joined an attack on Judah but were destroyed (2 Chronicles 20).
Ezekiel prophesied that Mount Seir would become desolate (Ezekiel 35).

name: Bozrah
what: A leading city of Edom, south of the Dead Sea.
today: Buseirah, in southern Jordan.
key: Jobab of Bozrah reigned as an early king of Edom (Genesis 36).
Isaiah announced that the Lord has a sacrifice in Bozrah (Isaiah 34).
Isaiah pictured the Lord coming from Bozrah in crimsoned garments (Isaiah 63).
Jeremiah warned that Bozrah would become a horror and a waste (Jeremiah 49).
Amos announced fire on the strongholds of Bozrah (Amos 1).

name: Mount Esau
what: The mountainous homeland of Edom, the nation descended from Esau.
today: The highlands of Edom, southern Jordan.
key: God declares he will destroy understanding from Mount Esau (Obadiah 1).
Everyone from Mount Esau will be cut off by slaughter (Obadiah 1).
Saviors will go up to Mount Zion to rule Mount Esau, and the kingdom will be the Lord's (Obadiah 1).

name: Esau
what: The land of Esau's descendants, Edom, sometimes called simply Esau or Mount Esau.
today: Southern Jordan, south and east of the Dead Sea.
key: Esau, also called Edom, settled with his descendants in the hill country of Seir (Genesis 36).
Jeremiah announces that God will bring calamity on Esau and strip him bare (Jeremiah 49).
Obadiah foretells judgment on Mount Esau for its violence against Judah (Obadiah 1).

name: Rameses
what: A city and district in the eastern Nile Delta, where Israel lived and from which the exodus began.
today: Likely Qantir, in the eastern Nile Delta, Egypt.
key: Joseph settles his family in the best of the land, the land of Rameses (Genesis 47).
Israel journeys from Rameses to Succoth at the exodus (Exodus 12).
Israel sets out from Rameses the day after the Passover (Numbers 33).

name: Tahpanhes
what: An Egyptian frontier city in the eastern Nile Delta, where Jeremiah was taken.
today: Tell Defenneh, in the northeastern Nile Delta, Egypt.
key: Judah's remnant took Jeremiah to Tahpanhes, where he hid stones at Pharaoh's palace (Jeremiah 43).
Jeremiah addressed the Jews living in Tahpanhes (Jeremiah 44).
Jeremiah told Tahpanhes to prepare for Babylon's attack (Jeremiah 46).

name: Hormah
what: A Canaanite town in the Negev whose name recalls its devotion to destruction.
today: Exact site uncertain; possibly Tel Masos, east of Beersheba.
key: Israel presumed to attack without God and was beaten back as far as Hormah (Numbers 14).
Israel devoted the Canaanite cities to destruction and named the place Hormah (Numbers 21).
Judah and Simeon destroyed Zephath and called it Hormah (Judges 1).
David sent plunder from the Amalekites to Hormah (1 Samuel 30).

name: Zephath
what: A Canaanite town in the Negev that Judah and Simeon destroyed and renamed Hormah.
today: Exact site uncertain; in the northern Negev near Beersheba, Israel.
key: Judah and Simeon struck the Canaanites in Zephath and devoted it to destruction (Judges 1).
The city was then called Hormah (Judges 1).

name: Mount Halak
what: A bare mountain in the south rising toward Seir, the southern limit of Joshua's conquest.
today: Likely Jebel Halaq in the northern Negev, southern Israel.
key: Joshua's conquest reached from Mount Halak in the south to Baal-gad in the north (Joshua 11).
Mount Halak is named again as the southern edge of the land whose kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).

name: Zoar
what: A small city near the southern end of the Dead Sea, spared when Sodom was destroyed.
today: Likely near Safi, southeast of the Dead Sea in Jordan.
key: Lot chose the well-watered Jordan Valley stretching toward Zoar (Genesis 13).
The king of Bela, that is, Zoar, fought against the four kings (Genesis 14).
Lot fled to Zoar, which God spared, before fire fell on Sodom (Genesis 19).
From Mount Nebo, Moses viewed the land as far as Zoar (Deuteronomy 34).
Isaiah pictured Moab's fugitives fleeing to Zoar (Isaiah 15).

name: Bela
what: The earlier name of Zoar, a small city near the southern end of the Dead Sea.
today: Likely near Safi, southeast of the Dead Sea in Jordan.
key: The king of Bela, that is, Zoar, joined Sodom's alliance against Chedorlaomer and his allies (Genesis 14).
The five kings were defeated in the Valley of Siddim, and Lot was taken captive (Genesis 14).
Lot fled to Zoar, which God spared when fire fell on Sodom (Genesis 19).

name: Azmon
what: A place on the southern border of the promised land, near the Brook of Egypt.
today: Exact site unknown; possibly in the northeastern Sinai Peninsula.
key: The southern boundary turns from Azmon to the Brook of Egypt (Numbers 34).
Judah's southern boundary passes along to Azmon (Joshua 15).

name: Chaldea
what: Southern Mesopotamia, the homeland of the Chaldeans who ruled Babylon.
today: Southern Iraq.
key: Isaiah called the exiles to go out from Babylon and flee from Chaldea (Isaiah 48).
Jeremiah announced that Chaldea would be plundered (Jeremiah 50).
The Spirit brought Ezekiel in a vision to the exiles in Chaldea (Ezekiel 11).
Ezekiel rebuked Jerusalem for seeking alliances with Chaldea (Ezekiel 23).

name: Ur
what: A city in southern Mesopotamia, the original home of Abraham's family.
today: Tell el-Muqayyar, in southern Iraq.
key: Haran dies in Ur, and Terah takes Abram from Ur toward Canaan (Genesis 11).
The Lord reminds Abram that he brought him out from Ur of the Chaldeans (Genesis 15).
The Levites praise God for choosing Abram and bringing him out of Ur (Nehemiah 9).

name: Zoan
what: An ancient royal city in the northeastern Nile Delta of Egypt.
today: San el-Hagar (ancient Tanis), in the northeastern Nile Delta, Egypt.
key: Hebron was built seven years before Zoan in Egypt (Numbers 13).
God worked his wonders against Egypt in the fields of Zoan (Psalms 78).
Isaiah called the princes of Zoan foolish counselors (Isaiah 19).
Judah's envoys went to Zoan seeking Egypt's help (Isaiah 30).
Ezekiel foretold that God would set fire to Zoan (Ezekiel 30).

name: Beer
what: A stopping place in Moab where God gave Israel water from a well during the wilderness journey.
today: Exact site unknown; north of the Arnon River in Jordan.
key: The Lord told Moses to gather the people at Beer so he could give them water (Numbers 21).
Israel sang a song to the well that the princes and nobles had dug (Numbers 21).

name: Brook of Egypt
what: A seasonal stream marking the southwestern border of the Promised Land.
today: Likely Wadi el-Arish in northern Sinai, Egypt.
key: The Brook of Egypt formed the southern boundary of the land (Numbers 34).
Judah's border ended at the Brook of Egypt (Joshua 15).
All Israel from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt celebrated the temple's dedication (1 Kings 8).
Babylon took all Egypt's territory from the Brook of Egypt to the Euphrates (2 Kings 24).
Ezekiel's restored land extends to the Brook of Egypt (Ezekiel 47).

name: Valley of Salt
what: A valley in the south, near Edom's border, where Judah's armies defeated the Edomites.
today: Exact site uncertain; possibly south of the Dead Sea.
key: David strikes down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt (2 Samuel 8).
Amaziah strikes down ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt (2 Kings 14).
Abishai strikes down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt (1 Chronicles 18).
Amaziah leads his people to the Valley of Salt and defeats the men of Seir (2 Chronicles 25).

name: Admah
what: One of the cities of the valley destroyed with Sodom and Gomorrah.
today: Exact site unknown; likely near the southern Dead Sea.
key: Admah marked part of the territory of the Canaanites (Genesis 10).
The king of Admah joined the cities of the valley in war (Genesis 14).
Moses recalled that God overthrew Admah with Sodom in his anger (Deuteronomy 29).
God asked how he could make Israel like Admah (Hosea 11).

name: Zeboiim
what: One of the cities of the plain near Sodom and Gomorrah, destroyed in God's judgment.
today: Exact site unknown; probably near the southern Dead Sea.
key: Zeboiim is listed near Sodom and Gomorrah on the edge of Canaanite territory (Genesis 10).
Shemeber king of Zeboiim joins the kings of the valley against Chedorlaomer (Genesis 14).
Moses warns that disobedience could leave the land like Zeboiim, which the Lord overthrew (Deuteronomy 29).
God asks how he could make Israel like Zeboiim, showing his compassion (Hosea 11).

name: Gomorrah
what: A city near Sodom destroyed by God with fire for its wickedness.
today: Exact site unknown; probably near the Dead Sea
key: The king of Gomorrah was defeated in the war of the kings (Genesis 14).
The LORD rained sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19).
Isaiah compared the rulers of Judah to the rulers of Gomorrah (Isaiah 1).
Jude cites Sodom and Gomorrah as an example of eternal fire (Jude 1).

name: Moladah
what: A town in the Negev of Judah, later allotted to Simeon and resettled after the exile.
today: Exact site uncertain; in the Negev east of Beersheba, Israel.
key: Moladah is listed among the southern towns of Judah (Joshua 15).
Moladah is allotted to the tribe of Simeon (Joshua 19).
Moladah appears among the towns where Simeon's descendants lived (1 Chronicles 4).
Men of Judah live in Moladah after the return from exile (Nehemiah 11).

name: Ziph
what: A town in the Negev of Judah toward Edom, distinct from Ziph near Hebron.
today: Exact site unknown; in the Negev of southern Israel.
key: Ziph is listed among Judah's southernmost towns toward the border of Edom (Joshua 15).
A different Ziph appears later in the same list among the hill-country towns (Joshua 15).

name: Kir
what: A distant land, probably in Mesopotamia, from which the Arameans came and to which Assyria exiled them.
today: Exact site unknown; likely in Mesopotamia.
key: Assyria captured Damascus and carried its people to Kir (2 Kings 16).
Isaiah also names Kir of Moab, a separate Moabite city (Isaiah 15).
Kir took up the shield against Jerusalem (Isaiah 22).
Amos foretold that Aram's people would go into exile to Kir (Amos 1).
God reminded Israel that he brought the Arameans from Kir (Amos 9).

name: Kabzeel
what: A town in the Negev of southern Judah, home of David's mighty man Benaiah.
today: Exact site unknown; in the Negev of southern Israel.
key: Kabzeel is listed among Judah's southernmost towns toward Edom (Joshua 15).
Benaiah of Kabzeel, one of David's mighty men, struck down two champions of Moab (2 Samuel 23).
The Chronicler repeats Benaiah's deeds and his hometown of Kabzeel (1 Chronicles 11).

name: Sodom
what: A city in the Jordan valley destroyed by God for its great wickedness.
today: Exact site unknown; probably near the Dead Sea
key: Lot chose the Jordan valley and moved his tent as far as Sodom (Genesis 13).
Abraham pleaded with the LORD to spare Sodom for the sake of the righteous (Genesis 18).
The LORD rained sulfur and fire on Sodom after rescuing Lot (Genesis 19).
Jesus said judgment would be more bearable for Sodom than for unrepentant towns (Matthew 11).
Peter cites Sodom's destruction as an example of God's judgment (2 Peter 2).

name: Hazar-shual
what: A town in the Negev of Judah, later allotted to Simeon and resettled after the exile.
today: Exact site unknown; in the Negev near Beersheba, Israel.
key: Hazar-shual is listed among the southern towns of Judah (Joshua 15).
Hazar-shual is allotted to the tribe of Simeon (Joshua 19).
Hazar-shual appears among the towns where Simeon's descendants lived (1 Chronicles 4).
Men of Judah live in Hazar-shual after the return from exile (Nehemiah 11).

name: Alexandria
what: A great Egyptian seaport founded by Alexander the Great, a center of Jewish learning and grain shipping.
today: Alexandria, on the Mediterranean coast of Egypt.
key: Apollos, a native of Alexandria, comes to Ephesus (Acts 18).
Paul's centurion finds an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and puts them aboard (Acts 27).
After the shipwreck, Paul sails on an Alexandrian ship that wintered at Malta (Acts 28).

name: Valley of Siddim
what: A valley by the Salt Sea where four kings defeated the five kings of the plain.
today: Likely near the southern end of the Dead Sea; exact site unknown.
key: The five kings, including those of Sodom and Gomorrah, joined forces in the Valley of Siddim (Genesis 14).
The valley was full of bitumen pits, and fleeing kings fell into them (Genesis 14).

name: Beersheba
what: A town in the Negeb at the southern edge of Israel, linked with the patriarchs.
today: Tel Beersheba, near Beersheba, Israel
key: Abraham made a covenant with Abimelech over a well at Beersheba (Genesis 21).
The LORD appeared to Isaac at Beersheba and renewed his promise (Genesis 26).
Jacob offered sacrifices at Beersheba on his way to Egypt (Genesis 46).
All Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew Samuel was a prophet (1 Samuel 3).
Elijah fled to Beersheba to escape Jezebel (1 Kings 19).

name: Baalah
what: A town in Judah's far south toward Edom, later counted among Simeon's towns; not the Baalah that is Kiriath-jearim.
today: Exact site unknown; in the Negeb near Beersheba, southern Israel.
key: Baalah is listed among Judah's southernmost towns in the Negeb toward Edom (Joshua 15).
Balah, likely the same town, was included in Simeon's inheritance within Judah (Joshua 19).
Simeon's descendants lived in Bilhah and nearby towns until David's reign (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Arad
what: A Canaanite royal city in the Negev whose king attacked Israel in the wilderness.
today: Tel Arad, in the northeastern Negev, Israel.
key: The king of Arad attacks Israel, and Israel devotes his cities to destruction (Numbers 21).
The Canaanite king of Arad hears that Israel is coming (Numbers 33).
The king of Arad is listed among the kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).
The Kenites settle among the people in the Negev near Arad (Judges 1).

name: Horonaim
what: A town of Moab named in prophecies of Moab's destruction.
today: Exact site unknown; in Moab, Jordan.
key: Isaiah describes a cry of destruction on the road to Horonaim (Isaiah 15).
Jeremiah foretells the cry of desolation and great destruction from Horonaim (Jeremiah 48).

name: Zanoah
what: A town in the hill country of Judah, distinct from the Zanoah in the lowland.
today: Likely Khirbet Zanuta, southwest of Hebron, West Bank.
key: Zanoah is listed among Judah's towns in the hill country, near Jezreel and Kain (Joshua 15).
Jekuthiel is named as the father, likely the founder, of Zanoah (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Ain
what: A town in the far south of Judah, later assigned to Simeon and listed as a Levitical city.
today: Exact site unknown; in the Negev near Rimmon, southern Israel.
key: Ain is listed among the southernmost towns of Judah (Joshua 15).
Ain is allotted to the tribe of Simeon within Judah's territory (Joshua 19).
Ain is given to the Levites as one of their cities (Joshua 21).
Ain appears among the towns where the descendants of Simeon lived (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Eshtemoa
what: A town in the hill country of Judah south of Hebron, given to the priests.
today: Modern as-Samu, south of Hebron.
key: Eshtemoa was given to the descendants of Aaron the priest (Joshua 21).
David sent some of the Amalekite spoil to the elders of Eshtemoa (1 Samuel 30).
Eshtemoa appears again among the priests' towns (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Ziklag
what: A town in the Negev given to David by the Philistine king Achish.
today: Possibly Tel Sera or Tel Halif in the northwestern Negev, Israel.
key: Ziklag was allotted to Judah and then to Simeon (Joshua 19).
Achish king of Gath gave Ziklag to David as he fled from Saul (1 Samuel 27).
Amalekites burned Ziklag, and David pursued them and recovered everything (1 Samuel 30).
At Ziklag, David received news of Saul's death (2 Samuel 1).
Mighty men came to join David at Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12).

name: Gerar
what: A town in the western Negev ruled by Abimelech in the patriarchs' time.
today: Likely Tel Haror, between Gaza and Beersheba in Israel.
key: The Canaanites' territory extended toward Gerar (Genesis 10).
Abraham called Sarah his sister to Abimelech king of Gerar, and God protected her (Genesis 20).
Isaac lived in Gerar during a famine and reopened wells amid disputes (Genesis 26).
Asa pursued the defeated Ethiopians as far as Gerar (2 Chronicles 14).

name: Besor
what: A brook in southwestern Judah that David's men crossed while pursuing the Amalekite raiders.
today: Likely Nahal Besor (Wadi Ghazzeh), flowing toward the coast near Gaza.
key: Two hundred of David's men were too exhausted to cross the brook Besor and stayed behind (1 Samuel 30).
After the victory, David ruled that those who stayed by the baggage would share equally in the spoil (1 Samuel 30).

name: Jattir
what: A town in the hill country of Judah given to the priests.
today: Khirbet Attir, south of Hebron, West Bank.
key: Jattir is listed among the towns of the hill country of Judah (Joshua 15).
Jattir is given to the descendants of Aaron (Joshua 21).
David sends spoil from the Amalekites to the elders of Jattir (1 Samuel 30).
Jattir is listed again among the priests' cities (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Debir
what: A Canaanite city in the hill country of Judah, southwest of Hebron.
today: Possibly Khirbet Rabud, southwest of Hebron in the West Bank.
key: Joshua captured Debir and struck down its king (Joshua 10).
Joshua cut off the Anakim from Debir (Joshua 11).
Othniel captured Debir and received Caleb's daughter Achsah as his wife (Joshua 15).
Debir was given to the priests as a Levitical city (Joshua 21).

name: Kiriath-sepher
what: The earlier name of Debir, a town in Judah captured by Othniel.
today: Debir, possibly Khirbet Rabud, southwest of Hebron, West Bank.
key: Caleb offers his daughter Achsah to whoever captures Kiriath-sepher (Joshua 15).
Othniel captures Kiriath-sepher and marries Achsah (Joshua 15).
Judges retells Othniel's capture of Kiriath-sepher, formerly the name of Debir (Judges 1).

name: Maon
what: A town in the hill country of Judah with a nearby wilderness where David hid from Saul.
today: Khirbet Ma'in, south of Hebron, West Bank.
key: Maon is listed among the towns of the hill country of Judah (Joshua 15).
Saul pursues David in the wilderness of Maon (1 Samuel 23).
Nabal, Abigail's husband, lives in Maon (1 Samuel 25).

name: Rock of Escape
what: A rock in the wilderness of Maon where David narrowly escaped Saul.
today: Exact site unknown; in the wilderness of Maon, south of Hebron.
key: David goes down to the rock in the wilderness of Maon as Saul closes in (1 Samuel 23).
Saul breaks off pursuit to face a Philistine raid, so the place is called the Rock of Escape (1 Samuel 23).

name: Arnon
what: A deep river gorge flowing into the Dead Sea, forming Moab's northern border.
today: Wadi Mujib in Jordan, east of the Dead Sea.
key: Israel camped beyond the Arnon, the boundary between Moab and the Amorites (Numbers 21).
Balak met Balaam at a city on the Arnon (Numbers 22).
Jephthah reminded the Ammonites that Israel had never crossed the Arnon into Moab (Judges 11).
Jeremiah announced Moab's destruction to be proclaimed by the Arnon (Jeremiah 48).

name: Valley of the Arnon
what: The deep gorge of the Arnon River, forming the southern border of Israel's land east of the Jordan.
today: Wadi Mujib in Jordan, east of the Dead Sea.
key: God told Israel to cross the Valley of the Arnon and fight Sihon (Deuteronomy 2).
Israel took the land from the Valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon (Deuteronomy 3).
Reuben's territory began at Aroer on the edge of the Valley of the Arnon (Joshua 13).
Hazael of Syria struck Israel's land as far as the Valley of the Arnon (2 Kings 10).

name: Carmel
what: A town in the hill country of Judah, south of Hebron, home of Nabal and Abigail.
today: Likely Khirbet el-Kirmil, south of Hebron, West Bank
key: Saul set up a monument for himself at Carmel (1 Samuel 15).
Nabal, a wealthy man of Carmel, refused David's request, and Abigail intervened (1 Samuel 25).
Abigail, widow of Nabal of Carmel, went with David to Hebron (2 Samuel 2).
Hezro of Carmel was one of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23).

name: Ar
what: A chief city of Moab near the Arnon River, given by God to the descendants of Lot.
today: Exact site unknown; likely near the Arnon in Jordan.
key: The Amorites' victory song says fire consumed Ar of Moab (Numbers 21).
God told Israel not to harass Moab, for he had given Ar to Lot's descendants (Deuteronomy 2).
Isaiah lamented that Ar of Moab was laid waste in a night (Isaiah 15).

name: Goshen
what: A district and town in the southern hill country of Judah, distinct from Goshen in Egypt.
today: Exact site unknown; in the hill country south of Hebron.
key: Joshua struck the land from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza and all the country of Goshen (Joshua 10).
Goshen is listed among the regions Joshua took in the south (Joshua 11).
A town named Goshen appears among Judah's hill-country towns (Joshua 15).

name: Horesh
what: A place in the wilderness of Ziph where David hid from Saul.
today: Possibly Khirbet Khoreisa, south of Hebron, West Bank.
key: David hides at Horesh in the wilderness of Ziph while Saul seeks his life (1 Samuel 23).
Jonathan meets David at Horesh and strengthens his hand in God (1 Samuel 23).
The Ziphites tell Saul that David is hiding at Horesh (1 Samuel 23).

name: Rock of Escape
what: A rocky place in the Wilderness of Maon where Saul nearly caught David.
today: Exact site unknown; in the Wilderness of Maon south of Hebron, West Bank.
key: Saul's men were closing in on David on the other side of the mountain (1 Samuel 23).
Saul broke off pursuit to face a Philistine raid, so the place is called the Rock of Escape (1 Samuel 23).

name: En-gedi
what: A spring-fed oasis on the western shore of the Dead Sea in the wilderness of Judah.
today: Ein Gedi, on the western shore of the Dead Sea, Israel.
key: En-gedi was one of Judah's towns in the wilderness (Joshua 15).
David hid in the strongholds of En-gedi while fleeing Saul (1 Samuel 23).
David spared Saul's life in a cave at En-gedi (1 Samuel 24).
Moabite and Ammonite armies gathered at Hazazon-tamar, that is, En-gedi (2 Chronicles 20).
Ezekiel saw fishermen standing beside the healed sea from En-gedi (Ezekiel 47).

name: Jeshimon
what: A barren wasteland in Judah, near which David hid from Saul.
today: The Judean wilderness west of the Dead Sea, West Bank.
key: The Ziphites say David hides on the hill of Hachilah, south of Jeshimon (1 Samuel 23).
David stays in the wilderness of Maon, south of Jeshimon (1 Samuel 23).
Saul camps on the hill of Hachilah beside Jeshimon while hunting David (1 Samuel 26).

name: Hazazon-tamar
what: An oasis on the western shore of the Dead Sea, identified in Chronicles with En-gedi.
today: En-gedi, on the western shore of the Dead Sea, Israel.
key: Chedorlaomer and his allies defeated the Amorites living in Hazazon-tamar (Genesis 14).
A Moabite and Ammonite army gathered at Hazazon-tamar, that is, En-gedi, against Jehoshaphat (2 Chronicles 20).
After Jehoshaphat sought the Lord, the invading armies turned and destroyed one another (2 Chronicles 20).

name: Hachilah
what: A hill in the wilderness near Ziph where David hid from Saul.
today: Exact site unknown; in the Judean wilderness southeast of Hebron.
key: The Ziphites told Saul that David was hiding on the hill of Hachilah (1 Samuel 23).
Saul camped on the hill of Hachilah, and David spared his life while he slept (1 Samuel 26).

name: Aroer
what: A town on the north rim of the Arnon gorge east of the Dead Sea.
today: Khirbet Ara'ir, on the northern edge of Wadi Mujib, Jordan.
key: Israel took every city from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon to Gilead (Deuteronomy 2).
Aroer marked the southern edge of Reuben's territory (Joshua 13).
Jephthah said Israel had lived in Aroer for three hundred years (Judges 11).
Hazael of Syria struck Israel as far as Aroer (2 Kings 10).
Jeremiah told the people of Aroer to watch for Moab's fleeing refugees (Jeremiah 48).

name: Ziph
what: A town in the hill country of Judah, southeast of Hebron, beside a wilderness.
today: Tell Zif, southeast of Hebron in the West Bank.
key: Ziph was allotted to Judah in the hill country (Joshua 15).
Jonathan strengthened David in the wilderness of Ziph, but Ziphites betrayed him (1 Samuel 23).
David took Saul's spear and water jar in the wilderness of Ziph (1 Samuel 26).
Rehoboam fortified Ziph (2 Chronicles 11).

name: Moab
what: A kingdom east of the Dead Sea, descended from Lot and often hostile to Israel.
today: West-central Jordan, east of the Dead Sea
key: Balak king of Moab hired Balaam to curse Israel, but he blessed them instead (Numbers 22).
Moses died in the land of Moab after viewing the promised land (Deuteronomy 34).
Ehud killed Eglon king of Moab and freed Israel (Judges 3).
Ruth the Moabite returned with Naomi to Bethlehem (Ruth 1).
Mesha king of Moab rebelled against Israel after Ahab died (2 Kings 3).

name: Dibon
what: A Moabite town north of the Arnon, later held by Israel.
today: Dhiban, in central Jordan north of Wadi Mujib.
key: Israel's victory over Sihon brought Heshbon's land as far as Dibon (Numbers 21).
The Gadites rebuilt Dibon (Numbers 32).
Moses allotted Dibon to Reuben (Joshua 13).
Isaiah pictured Dibon going up to its high places to weep (Isaiah 15).
Jeremiah announced Dibon's humiliation in Moab's judgment (Jeremiah 48).

name: Oboth
what: A stopping place of Israel near the border of Moab during the wilderness journey.
today: Exact site unknown; south or east of the Dead Sea, Jordan.
key: After the bronze serpent, Israel sets out and camps at Oboth (Numbers 21).
Oboth is recorded among Israel's wilderness camps (Numbers 33).

name: Valley of Hamon-gog
what: A valley in Ezekiel's prophecy where the armies of Gog will be buried.
today: A prophetic location east of the sea; no known site.
key: God gives Gog a burial place in the Valley of the Travelers, renamed Hamon-gog (Ezekiel 39).
Israel will spend seven months burying the dead to cleanse the land (Ezekiel 39).
Searchers mark any bone they find so buriers can carry it to the valley (Ezekiel 39).

name: Eglon
what: A Canaanite city in the Shephelah of southern Judah.
today: Exact site uncertain; possibly Tell Aitun or Tel Hesi in southern Israel.
key: Debir king of Eglon joined four other Amorite kings against Gibeon (Joshua 10).
Joshua captured Eglon and devoted it to destruction (Joshua 10).
The king of Eglon is listed among the kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).
Eglon was allotted to Judah (Joshua 15).

name: Kain
what: A town in the hill country of Judah, listed near Zanoah, Gibeah, and Timnah.
today: Possibly Khirbet Yaqin, southeast of Hebron.
key: Kain is listed with Gibeah and Timnah among the hill-country towns of Judah (Joshua 15).
It belonged to a group of ten towns with their villages, including Maon, Carmel, and Ziph (Joshua 15).

name: Jahaz
what: A town on the plateau east of the Dead Sea where Israel defeated Sihon.
today: Exact site uncertain; possibly Khirbet el-Medeiyineh, Jordan.
key: Sihon king of the Amorites fought Israel at Jahaz and was defeated (Numbers 21).
Moses recalled the victory over Sihon at Jahaz (Deuteronomy 2).
Jephthah reminded the Ammonites of Sihon's defeat at Jahaz (Judges 11).
Jeremiah named Jahaz among the Moabite cities facing judgment (Jeremiah 48).

name: Machpelah
what: A field and cave near Mamre that Abraham bought as a family burial place.
today: Traditionally the Cave of the Patriarchs in Hebron.
key: Abraham bought the field and cave of Machpelah from Ephron the Hittite to bury Sarah (Genesis 23).
Isaac and Ishmael buried Abraham in the cave of Machpelah (Genesis 25).
Jacob asked to be buried there with Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, and Leah (Genesis 49).
Jacob's sons carried his body from Egypt and buried him at Machpelah (Genesis 50).

name: Gaza
what: The southernmost of the five main Philistine cities, on the coastal road to Egypt.
today: Gaza City, Gaza Strip
key: Gaza marked the southwestern border of the Canaanites (Genesis 10).
Samson carried off the doors of Gaza's city gate (Judges 16).
Samson died in Gaza, pulling down the temple of Dagon (Judges 16).
Amos announced judgment on Gaza for selling captives to Edom (Amos 1).
Philip met an Ethiopian official on the road from Jerusalem to Gaza (Acts 8).

name: Hebron
what: An ancient city in the hill country of Judah, linked with Abraham and David's early reign.
today: Hebron, West Bank
key: Abraham buried Sarah in the cave of Machpelah near Hebron (Genesis 23).
Caleb received Hebron as his inheritance (Joshua 14).
David was anointed king over Judah at Hebron (2 Samuel 2).
All the tribes came to Hebron and anointed David king over Israel (2 Samuel 5).
Absalom began his rebellion against David at Hebron (2 Samuel 15).

name: Jezreel
what: A town in the hill country of Judah, home of David's wife Ahinoam.
today: Exact site unknown; in the hill country south of Hebron.
key: Jezreel was a town in the hill country of Judah (Joshua 15).
David married Ahinoam of Jezreel (1 Samuel 25).
Ahinoam of Jezreel was among David's wives captured at Ziklag (1 Samuel 30).
Amnon, David's firstborn, was son of Ahinoam of Jezreel (2 Samuel 3).

name: Kiriath-arba
what: The older name of Hebron, a city in the hill country of Judah named after Arba of the Anakim.
today: Hebron, in the southern West Bank.
key: Sarah died at Kiriath-arba, and Abraham mourned for her (Genesis 23).
Jacob returned to his father Isaac at Kiriath-arba, where Isaac died (Genesis 35).
Joshua gave Hebron, formerly Kiriath-arba, to Caleb as his inheritance (Joshua 14).
Judah defeated Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai there (Judges 1).
Some people of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba after the exile (Nehemiah 11).

name: Salt Sea
what: The Dead Sea, the salty lake at the lowest point of the Jordan Valley.
today: The Dead Sea, between Israel, the West Bank, and Jordan.
key: Four kings fought five kings in the Valley of Siddim, that is, the Salt Sea (Genesis 14).
The Salt Sea formed part of the eastern boundary of the land (Numbers 34).
When Israel crossed the Jordan, the waters flowing to the Salt Sea were cut off (Joshua 3).
Judah's boundary began at the southern end of the Salt Sea (Joshua 15).

name: Sea of the Arabah
what: The salt lake at the south end of the Jordan Valley, today called the Dead Sea.
today: The Dead Sea, between Israel, the West Bank, and Jordan.
key: Waters flowing toward the Sea of the Arabah were cut off as Israel crossed the Jordan (Joshua 3).
Jeroboam II restored Israel's border from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, as Jonah foretold (2 Kings 14).

name: Mamre
what: A place near Hebron where Abraham lived, facing the cave of Machpelah.
today: Near Hebron; possibly Ramat el-Khalil, just north of the city.
key: The cave of Machpelah that Abraham bought lay east of Mamre (Genesis 23).
Abraham was buried in the cave east of Mamre (Genesis 25).
Jacob came home to Isaac at Mamre, where Isaac died (Genesis 35).
Jacob was buried in the field east of Mamre (Genesis 50).

name: Valley of Eshcol
what: A valley near Hebron where the twelve spies cut a huge cluster of grapes.
today: Near Hebron, West Bank; exact site unknown.
key: The spies cut a cluster of grapes so large two men carry it on a pole (Numbers 13).
Moses recalls that the spies saw Eshcol yet discouraged Israel from entering the land (Numbers 32).
Moses retells how the spies reached the Valley of Eshcol and brought back fruit (Deuteronomy 1).

name: Lachish
what: A major fortified city in the lowlands of Judah, southwest of Jerusalem.
today: Tel Lachish, Israel
key: Joshua captured Lachish after defeating its king and his allies (Joshua 10).
King Amaziah fled to Lachish and was killed there (2 Kings 14).
Hezekiah sent tribute to Sennacherib, who was at Lachish (2 Kings 18).
Lachish and Azekah were the last fortified cities of Judah left against Babylon (Jeremiah 34).

name: Libnah
what: A fortified town in the lowlands of Judah, southwest of Jerusalem.
today: Exact site uncertain; possibly Tel Burna, Israel
key: Joshua captured Libnah during his southern campaign (Joshua 10).
Libnah was given to the priests as a Levitical city (Joshua 21).
Libnah revolted against King Jehoram of Judah (2 Kings 8).
Sennacherib's army was fighting against Libnah when he sent threats to Hezekiah (2 Kings 19).

name: Kiriathaim
what: A town on the plateau east of the Dead Sea, built up by Reuben and later held by Moab.
today: Exact site uncertain; possibly Khirbet el-Qureiyat, Jordan.
key: The Reubenites rebuilt Kiriathaim (Numbers 32).
It was allotted to Reuben (Joshua 13).
Jeremiah announced that Kiriathaim would be shamed and captured (Jeremiah 48).
Ezekiel named Kiriathaim among the glorious cities of Moab facing judgment (Ezekiel 25).

name: Beth-zur
what: A town in the hill country of Judah, north of Hebron, guarding the southern approach to Jerusalem.
today: Khirbet et-Tubeiqah, about four miles north of Hebron.
key: Beth-zur is listed among the towns of Judah's hill country (Joshua 15).
King Rehoboam fortified Beth-zur as one of Judah's defensive cities (2 Chronicles 11).
A ruler of half the district of Beth-zur helped repair Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3).

name: Mareshah
what: A town in the lowland of Judah, southwest of Jerusalem.
today: Tel Maresha, near Beit Guvrin, Israel.
key: Mareshah was allotted to Judah in the lowland (Joshua 15).
Rehoboam fortified Mareshah (2 Chronicles 11).
Asa defeated Zerah the Cushite's vast army near Mareshah (2 Chronicles 14).
Eliezer of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat's alliance with Ahaziah (2 Chronicles 20).
Micah warned that a conqueror would come against Mareshah (Micah 1).

name: Moresheth
what: A town in Judah's lowland, the hometown of the prophet Micah.
today: Likely Tell el-Judeideh, near Beit Guvrin in the Shephelah, Israel.
key: The word of the LORD came to Micah of Moresheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah (Micah 1).
In his lament over Judah's towns, Micah named Moresheth-gath (Micah 1).
Elders recalled Micah of Moresheth, whose warning moved Hezekiah to seek the LORD (Jeremiah 26).

name: Nebo
what: A town in Judah whose people returned from exile, distinct from Mount Nebo in Moab.
today: Exact site uncertain; possibly modern Nuba, northwest of Hebron.
key: The men of Nebo are counted among the exiles returning from Babylon (Ezra 2).
Some descendants of Nebo had married foreign women and agreed to put them away (Ezra 10).
Nehemiah's list counts the men of the other Nebo among the returnees (Nehemiah 7).

name: Valley of Beracah
what: A valley near Tekoa where Judah praised God after he defeated the invading armies.
today: Likely Wadi Berekut, near Tekoa south of Bethlehem, West Bank.
key: Jehoshaphat led Judah in prayer, and God made the invading armies destroy one another (2 Chronicles 20).
After three days of gathering spoil, Judah assembled in the valley and blessed the Lord (2 Chronicles 20).

name: Keilah
what: A fortified town in the lowlands of Judah, northwest of Hebron.
today: Khirbet Qila, southwest of Bethlehem, West Bank
key: David rescued Keilah from the Philistines but fled when its people might betray him (1 Samuel 23).
Rulers of the district of Keilah helped repair Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3).

name: Giloh
what: A town in the hill country of Judah, home of David's counselor Ahithophel.
today: Exact site unknown; in the hill country of Judah, possibly near Hebron, West Bank.
key: Giloh is listed among the towns in the hill country of Judah (Joshua 15).
Absalom sent for Ahithophel from his city Giloh to join the conspiracy against David (2 Samuel 15).
When his advice was rejected, Ahithophel went home to his city and hanged himself (2 Samuel 17).

name: Tekoa
what: A town in the Judean hills south of Bethlehem, on the edge of the wilderness.
today: Khirbet Tequ', south of Bethlehem in the West Bank.
key: Joab brought a wise woman from Tekoa to persuade David to recall Absalom (2 Samuel 14).
Rehoboam fortified Tekoa as a defensive city of Judah (2 Chronicles 11).
Jehoshaphat's army marched into the wilderness of Tekoa and God gave victory (2 Chronicles 20).
Jeremiah called for a trumpet blast in Tekoa as disaster approached (Jeremiah 6).
Amos was among the shepherds of Tekoa when he prophesied (Amos 1).

name: Kedemoth
what: A town and wilderness east of the Dead Sea, later given to Reuben and the Levites.
today: Exact site uncertain; east of the Dead Sea, Jordan.
key: Moses sends messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon asking for passage (Deuteronomy 2).
Kedemoth is allotted to the tribe of Reuben (Joshua 13).
Kedemoth is given to the Merarite Levites (Joshua 21).
Kedemoth is listed again among the Levitical cities (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Adullam
what: A town in the Shephelah of Judah, known for a nearby cave where David hid.
today: Tel Adullam, in the Shephelah southwest of Bethlehem, Israel.
key: The king of Adullam was among the kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).
David escaped to the cave of Adullam, where about four hundred men joined him (1 Samuel 22).
Three of David's mighty men came to him at the cave of Adullam (2 Samuel 23).
Rehoboam fortified Adullam (2 Chronicles 11).
Micah foresaw Israel's glory fleeing to Adullam in judgment (Micah 1).

name: Beth-peor
what: A town in Moab near Mount Nebo, opposite the valley where Israel camped and Moses was buried.
today: Exact site unknown; near Mount Nebo in Jordan.
key: Israel remains in the valley opposite Beth-peor (Deuteronomy 3).
Moses sets the law before Israel in the valley opposite Beth-peor (Deuteronomy 4).
God buries Moses in a valley opposite Beth-peor, and his grave remains unknown (Deuteronomy 34).
Beth-peor is allotted to the tribe of Reuben (Joshua 13).

name: Ashkelon
what: One of the five chief cities of the Philistines, on the Mediterranean coast.
today: Tel Ashkelon, within the modern city of Ashkelon, Israel.
key: Judah captured Ashkelon after Joshua's death (Judges 1).
Samson killed thirty men of Ashkelon to pay a lost wager (Judges 14).
The Philistines sent a guilt offering to Israel for Ashkelon after taking the ark (1 Samuel 6).
David lamented Saul and Jonathan, urging that the news not reach Ashkelon (2 Samuel 1).
Several prophets announced judgment on Ashkelon (Zephaniah 2).

name: Beth-haccherem
what: A town of Judah near Jerusalem that served as a district center and a place for signal fires.
today: Possibly Ramat Rahel, between Jerusalem and Bethlehem
key: Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth-haccherem, repaired the Dung Gate (Nehemiah 3).
Jeremiah called for a signal raised over Beth-haccherem as disaster came from the north (Jeremiah 6).

name: Baal-meon
what: A town east of the Dead Sea, settled by Reuben and later held by Moab.
today: Likely modern Ma'in, southwest of Madaba in Jordan.
key: The Reubenites rebuilt Baal-meon and gave it a new name (Numbers 32).
Reubenite clans lived in the area from Aroer to Nebo and Baal-meon (1 Chronicles 5).
Ezekiel names Baal-meon among Moab's prized cities that God would open to invaders (Ezekiel 25).

name: Socoh
what: A town in Judah's lowland overlooking the Elah Valley, where the Philistines camped before Goliath's challenge.
today: Likely Khirbet Abbad (Tel Socho), in the Elah Valley, Israel.
key: Socoh is listed with Adullam and Azekah among the towns of Judah's lowland (Joshua 15).
The Philistines gathered at Socoh and camped between Socoh and Azekah before Goliath's challenge (1 Samuel 17).
Rehoboam fortified Soco among his cities for defense in Judah (2 Chronicles 11).
In Ahaz's day the Philistines captured Soco with its villages (2 Chronicles 28).

name: Valley of Elah
what: A valley in the Shephelah of Judah where David fought Goliath.
today: The Elah Valley, west of Bethlehem near Azekah, Israel.
key: Saul's army camped in the Valley of Elah facing the Philistines, and David killed Goliath (1 Samuel 17).
At Nob the priest gave David the sword of Goliath, killed in the Valley of Elah (1 Samuel 21).

name: Pas-dammim
what: A place in Judah where the Philistines gathered for battle, called Ephes-dammim in the account of Goliath.
today: In the Elah Valley southwest of Bethlehem; exact site unknown.
key: Eleazar son of Dodo was with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines gathered there for battle (1 Chronicles 11).
They took their stand in a barley field, defended it, and the LORD saved them by a great victory (1 Chronicles 11).
Before Goliath's challenge, the Philistines camped between Socoh and Azekah, in Ephes-dammim (1 Samuel 17).

name: Canaan
what: The land between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean that God promised to Abraham's offspring.
today: Roughly modern Israel, the Palestinian territories, and Lebanon
key: Abram arrived in Canaan, and the LORD promised the land to his offspring (Genesis 12).
God promised all the land of Canaan as an everlasting possession (Genesis 17).
During a famine, Jacob sent his sons from Canaan to buy grain in Egypt (Genesis 42).
Moses sent twelve spies to explore the land of Canaan (Numbers 13).
Joshua and Eleazar distributed Canaan to the tribes of Israel (Joshua 14).

name: Gath
what: One of the five main Philistine cities, hometown of Goliath.
today: Likely Tell es-Safi (Tel Zafit), Israel
key: The ark was moved to Gath, and the LORD struck the city with tumors (1 Samuel 5).
Goliath of Gath challenged the armies of Israel (1 Samuel 17).
David pretended to be insane before Achish king of Gath (1 Samuel 21).
David lived among the Philistines under Achish of Gath (1 Samuel 27).
David lamented Saul and Jonathan, saying not to tell it in Gath (2 Samuel 1).

name: Timnah
what: A town in the hill country of Judah, distinct from the Timnah on Judah's northern border.
today: Exact site uncertain; in the hill country of Judah, West Bank.
key: Possibly the Timnah where Judah went up to shear his sheep and met Tamar (Genesis 38).
Timnah is listed with Kain and Gibeah among the hill-country towns of Judah (Joshua 15).

name: Chezib
what: A town in the lowlands of Judah where Judah's son Shelah was born.
today: Exact site unknown; in the Shephelah of Judah, Israel.
key: Judah's Canaanite wife bore his son Shelah while Judah was at Chezib (Genesis 38).
Achzib, likely the same town, was listed among Judah's lowland towns (Joshua 15).
Micah warned that the houses of Achzib would prove deceptive to Israel's kings (Micah 1).

name: Azekah
what: A fortified town in the Shephelah overlooking the Elah Valley.
today: Tel Azekah, above the Elah Valley in Israel.
key: God threw down great hailstones on the fleeing Amorites as far as Azekah (Joshua 10).
The Philistines camped between Socoh and Azekah when Goliath challenged Israel (1 Samuel 17).
Rehoboam fortified Azekah (2 Chronicles 11).
Lachish and Azekah were Judah's last fortified cities resisting Babylon (Jeremiah 34).

name: Bethlehem
what: A town in Judah south of Jerusalem, the hometown of David and birthplace of Jesus.
today: Bethlehem, West Bank
key: Rachel died and was buried on the way to Bethlehem (Genesis 35).
Naomi returned to Bethlehem with Ruth at the barley harvest (Ruth 1).
Samuel anointed David, Jesse's youngest son, in Bethlehem (1 Samuel 16).
Wise men came to Bethlehem to worship the newborn king (Matthew 2).
Angels announced Jesus' birth to shepherds near Bethlehem (Luke 2).

name: Ephrath
what: An older name for Bethlehem in Judah, near where Rachel died and was buried.
today: Bethlehem, south of Jerusalem.
key: Rachel died giving birth to Benjamin on the way to Ephrath, that is, Bethlehem (Genesis 35).
Jacob tells Joseph he buried Rachel on the way to Ephrath (Genesis 48).

name: Geruth Chimham
what: A lodging place near Bethlehem where the remnant of Judah stopped on the way to Egypt.
today: Exact site unknown; near Bethlehem
key: After Gedaliah's murder, Johanan and the remnant stayed at Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem (Jeremiah 41).
They meant to go on to Egypt because they feared the Chaldeans (Jeremiah 41).

name: Jarmuth
what: A Canaanite city in the lowland of Judah, west of Bethlehem.
today: Tel Yarmut, near Beit Shemesh, Israel.
key: Piram king of Jarmuth joined four other kings against Gibeon and was defeated (Joshua 10).
Jarmuth's king appears in the list of kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).
Jarmuth was allotted to Judah in the lowland (Joshua 15).
People of Judah resettled Jarmuth after the exile (Nehemiah 11).

name: Zanoah
what: A town in the lowland of Judah, resettled after the exile.
today: Likely Khirbet Zanu, near Beth-shemesh, Israel.
key: Zanoah is listed among Judah's towns, both in the lowland and the hill country (Joshua 15).
Hanun and the people of Zanoah repaired Jerusalem's Valley Gate (Nehemiah 3).
Returning exiles from Judah settled in Zanoah and its villages (Nehemiah 11).

name: Medeba
what: A town on the plateau east of the Dead Sea, south of Heshbon.
today: Madaba, Jordan.
key: The Amorites' victory song mentions Medeba (Numbers 21).
The plain of Medeba was allotted to Reuben (Joshua 13).
Ammon's hired Aramean forces camped before Medeba against David's army (1 Chronicles 19).
Isaiah pictured Moab wailing over Medeba (Isaiah 15).

name: Netophah
what: A village near Bethlehem in Judah, home of several of David's warriors.
today: Possibly Khirbet Bedd Faluh, southeast of Bethlehem.
key: Maharai and Heleb of Netophah were among David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
Maharai and Heldai of Netophah led monthly divisions of David's army (1 Chronicles 27).
Men of Netophah returned from exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).

name: Nebo
what: A town east of the Jordan near Mount Nebo, built up by Reuben and later held by Moab.
today: Likely Khirbet al-Mukhayyat, near Mount Nebo in Jordan.
key: The Reubenites rebuilt Nebo and settled there (Numbers 32).
Israel camped in the mountains of Abarim before Nebo (Numbers 33).
Reubenite clans lived from Aroer to Nebo and Baal-meon (1 Chronicles 5).
Isaiah pictured Moab wailing over Nebo (Isaiah 15).
Jeremiah announced judgment on Nebo among the cities of Moab (Jeremiah 48).

name: Minnith
what: An Ammonite town east of the Jordan, the limit of Jephthah's victory and known for its wheat.
today: Exact site unknown; east of the Jordan near Heshbon, Jordan.
key: Jephthah struck the Ammonites from Aroer to the neighborhood of Minnith, taking twenty cities (Judges 11).
Judah and Israel traded wheat of Minnith with Tyre (Ezekiel 27).

name: Beth-shemesh
what: A Levitical town on Judah's border with the Philistines, west of Jerusalem.
today: Tel Beth-Shemesh, west of Jerusalem, Israel
key: Beth-shemesh was given to the priests as a Levitical city (Joshua 21).
The ark returned on a cart to Beth-shemesh, where some men looked into it (1 Samuel 6).
Jehoash of Israel defeated and captured Amaziah of Judah at Beth-shemesh (2 Kings 14).
The Philistines captured Beth-shemesh during King Ahaz's reign (2 Chronicles 28).

name: Lehi
what: A place in Judah where Samson killed a thousand Philistines with a donkey's jawbone.
today: Exact site unknown; in Judah near the Philistine border.
key: The Philistines camped at Lehi, and Samson killed a thousand men with a fresh jawbone (Judges 15).
When Samson grew thirsty, God split open a hollow at Lehi and water came out (Judges 15).

name: Valley of Rephaim
what: A broad valley southwest of Jerusalem on the border of Judah and Benjamin.
today: Southwest of Jerusalem's Old City, in Jerusalem.
key: The valley marked part of the boundary between Judah and Benjamin (Joshua 15).
David twice defeated the Philistines who spread out in the Valley of Rephaim (2 Samuel 5).
Philistines camped there when three mighty men brought David water from Bethlehem (2 Samuel 23).
Isaiah compared Israel's judgment to gleaning ears in the Valley of Rephaim (Isaiah 17).

name: Abarim
what: A mountain range east of the Dead Sea, including Mount Nebo.
today: The highlands east of the Dead Sea in Jordan.
key: God told Moses to climb a mountain of Abarim and view the land (Numbers 27).
Israel camped in the mountains of Abarim before Nebo (Numbers 33).
God sent Moses up Mount Nebo in the Abarim range to die (Deuteronomy 32).
Jeremiah told Jerusalem to cry out from Abarim (Jeremiah 22).

name: Mount Nebo
what: A mountain in Moab east of the Jordan, from which Moses viewed the promised land before he died.
today: Jebel Nebo, northwest of Madaba, Jordan.
key: God told Moses to climb Mount Nebo, view Canaan, and die there on the mountain (Deuteronomy 32).
Moses climbed Nebo to the top of Pisgah, and the Lord showed him the whole land (Deuteronomy 34).
Moses died in Moab, and God buried him in a grave no one knows (Deuteronomy 34).
